questions.q: A team needs T-SQL-based reporting over structured data with strict schema enforcement, and their BI tool needs a SQL endpoint. Which Fabric item fits?
options: Warehouse — it enforces schema and speaks full T-SQL
Lakehouse — because it's schema-flexible
Eventstream — because it handles structured data
KQL Database — because it supports queries
questions.explain: A Warehouse enforces schema and speaks full T-SQL, unlike a Lakehouse, which is schema-flexible and Spark-first (Fabric Lesson 11).

questions.q: What is the exam-relevant fact about OneLake that trips people up?
options: Every Lakehouse and Warehouse in a tenant stores its data in the same underlying OneLake account, automatically
OneLake is a separate product you must purchase for each workspace
OneLake only stores Lakehouse data, never Warehouse data
OneLake requires manual data copying between items
questions.explain: This is what makes Shortcuts and Direct Lake Mode possible — a Warehouse's data is also OneLake data underneath.

questions.q: What Fabric feature lets you reference data from another item without copying it?
options: A Shortcut
A capacity
A deployment pipeline
A role assignment
questions.explain: Shortcuts (Fabric Lesson 7) reference data in place across OneLake without duplicating it.

questions.q: What does a Fabric capacity/SKU control?
options: The compute and throughput ceiling a workspace is assigned to, which determines cost and performance
Which users can log into the tenant
The programming language available in notebooks
Whether Git integration is enabled
questions.explain: Capacities (Fabric Lesson 14) are the compute unit governing a workspace's cost and performance ceiling.

questions.q: What does Git integration with deployment pipelines enable in Fabric?
options: Promoting a workspace's content from dev to test to prod under version control
Automatically deleting old Lakehouse files
Bypassing the need for a Fabric capacity
Converting a Lakehouse into a Warehouse automatically
questions.explain: This is the same dev/test/prod discipline from Fabric & Real-Time Analytics Chapter 3, applied to Fabric workspace content.
